rationales.1: The lead gives the finding in plain numbers, the then-and-now panel restates it in large type on both sides, and the ink-to-ink summary line reduces it to three differences, all reachable without decoding the one chart.
rationales.2: The single drift chart plots the full September to October window with no truncation, names its finding in the lead, leaves the missing seasons as open shaded bands, and draws 2019 hollow.
rationales.3: The ink device carries the instrument boundary onto every figure on the page, the most thorough disclosure of the set, and gaps and the unverified reading are stated in the chart notes, the table, and the closing note; the mobile table clips its instrument and notes columns, leaving the null rows without reasons and the seam carried by year colour alone in that view.
rationales.4: The register is patient and place-loving, and gathering one quote from each instrument era is a purposeful frame; quarantining both quotes in their own section keeps them from serving the data where it moves.
rationales.5: Clear hierarchy with a real legend, a balanced two-column comparison, and stacking that holds up on mobile; the record table clips mid-word at 375 width, the one visible break in an otherwise disciplined setting.
rationales.6: A static read with no scroll dependency and no device that paces the reader, so the base content stands alone.
rationales.7: The signature, a ledger printed in two inks, is one sentence and reaches all layers, but it dramatises the caveat rather than the shift, so the finding in the headline is charted rather than made felt.
rationales.8: One break, the two-ink system, declared in a legend directly under the deck with mechanics left conventional; the ink meaning leans on colour in the mobile table view where the instrument column is not visible.
rationales.9: Specific and quiet, with the line about the record keeping human time as well as rain, though a fair share of the prose is spent explaining the ink device itself.
rationales.10: The central device is derived from a fact of the record rather than applied to it, since the two inks exist only because the instrument changed after 1996.
